title: Week 24 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “perfect competition”?
options: A model with many firms, identical products, easy entry, and price-taking behavior.
The process through which people develop political values, identities, and habits.
The First Amendment protection for religious belief and practice, subject to legal doctrine.
Testing a claim by comparing it with independent evidence.
questions.explanation: Perfect competition means a model with many firms, identical products, easy entry, and price-taking behavior.
choices: A model with many firms, identical products, easy entry, and price-taking behavior.

options: Revenue minus explicit and implicit costs.

A market with many firms selling differentiated products and relatively easy entry.
Knowledge, skill, health, and experience that affect productive capacity.

options: Output measured with prices adjusted to remove the effect of inflation.
A market dominated by a small number of interdependent firms.
The process through which one condition is expected to produce another.
The condition that available resources are insufficient to satisfy every possible want.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “monopoly”?
options: A market in which one firm supplies a product without close substitutes and entry is blocked.
A public institution managing monetary policy and supporting payment and financial stability functions.
A judicial opinion disagreeing with the majority’s result or reasoning.
A system combining markets with public regulation, provision, taxation, and social insurance.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “barrier to entry”?
options: The value of the best alternative forgone when a choice is made.
A request from the Confederation Congress to states for money or resources.
A legal, technological, financial, strategic, or structural obstacle to new competition.
A cost that changes with output.
questions.explanation: Barrier to entry means a legal, technological, financial, strategic, or structural obstacle to new competition.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “antitrust”?
options: Law and enforcement intended to protect competitive processes from unlawful restraints or monopolization.
Negotiation between workers acting together and an employer over compensation and conditions.
Government through representatives and civic institutions oriented toward the public good.
A method that does not privilege a political party or require ideological agreement.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 24 inquiry?
options: A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student identifies entry barriers and competitive effects before labeling a large firm an unlawful monopoly.
